nodes.speaker: The Kestrel
nodes.text: Cole Calloway. Adelaide Crow — the paperwork calls me the Kestrel. There's a warrant on you in three counties, and I've read every word of it twice.

choices.text: I don't draw on people. Ever.

nodes.speaker: The Kestrel
nodes.text: The fourth lost the form. Bureaucracy is the real outlaw. Now — I know your rule, and I don't intend to test it.

nodes.speaker: The Kestrel
nodes.text: I know. It's in the file, underlined, next to a note that says 'confirmed, irritatingly'. Which is why I propose something better.

nodes.speaker: The Kestrel
nodes.text: A contest. Targets only, nothing that breathes. Three rounds, each one sillier than the last. You win, I ride out and the counties hear the wind kept me. I win, you come along quiet and polite.

nodes.speaker: The Kestrel
nodes.text: Tips their hat and walks. Like civilised legends.

nodes.speaker: The Kestrel
nodes.text: Round one: the bottle on the barrel, down the street. After you.
